Executive Order No. 10634, as amended, relating to loans for facilities 
destroyed or damaged by a major disaster, is revoked.
5-107.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10634, signed 1955-08-25 (20 FR 6433), provides under the Defense Production Act of 1950 that, whenever financial assistance is not otherwise available on reasonable terms, loans (including participations and guarantees) under section 302 of that Act may be made to aid the reconstruction, rehabilitation or replacement of facilities destroyed or damaged by a major disaster, when the facilities are required for national defense as determined by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization. No own-terms sunset or condition ends it. Later events, each a change to the determining officer and not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments): (1) Executive Order 10773, signed 1958-07-01 (23 FR 5061). Section 3(a) provides that each reference in any prior Executive order to the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization is hereby "amended to refer to the Director of the" Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization. Before: the determination was made by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization; after: by the Director of the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization. The held Federal Register text covers only the order's first two printed pages (23 FR 5061-5062); the list in section 4(b) that names EO 10634 as item (14), and section 10, which makes the order effective as of July 1, 1958, are on the following page and are seen only in the American Presidency Project transcription, which is not a cited source. July 1, 1958 is also the signing date, so the date does not depend on that page. (2) Executive Order 11051, signed 1962-09-27 (27 FR 9683), section 601, which states that each reference to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization or to its Director in the listed orders is amended to refer to the Office of Emergency Planning and its Director; the list includes, as the OCR prints it, "E xecu tive O rder N o. 10634 o f August 25,1955". Before: the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization; after: the Director of the Office of Emergency Planning. EO 11051 has no effective-date wording, so its signing date is recorded. (3) Executive Order 11725, signed 1973-06-27 (38 FR 17175), section 3, which transfers to the Administrator of General Services all authority vested in the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness as of June 30, 1973, including functions under "(7 ) Executive Order No. 10634 of August 25, 1955, relating to loans" for defense facilities damaged by a major disaster; section 8 states "This order shall be effective as of July 1, 1973." Before: the determination rested with the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness; after: the authority rested with the Administrator of General Services. EO 11725 prints no replacement text for EO 10634. First end: Executive Order 12148, Federal Emergency Management, section 5-106: "Executive Order No. 10634, as amended, relating to loans for facilities" destroyed or damaged by a major disaster, is revoked. Its closing section states "This Order is effective July 15,1979." EO 12148 was signed 1979-07-20, so the stated effective date is retroactive; the first end is recorded on the stated effective date, 1979-07-15, and the signing date 1979-07-20 is the alternative reading. No held source shows an earlier lapse of the section 302 authority the order invokes.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10634 (20 FR 6433, Federal Register of September 1, 1955), signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower and dated August 25, 1955; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: one whole-order clause. Under the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, the order provides that, whenever financial assistance is not otherwise available on reasonable terms, loans (including participations in, or guarantees of, loans) under section 302 of that Act may be made to aid the reconstruction, rehabilitation or replacement of facilities destroyed or damaged by a major disaster, whenever the facilities are required for national defense as determined by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization. Later events (strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21, each recorded with date, actor, mechanism and before and after text): EO 10773 (effective July 1, 1958) amends every reference in prior orders to the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization to refer to the Director of the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization; EO 11051 section 601 (1962-09-27) amends the references in this order to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization and its Director to refer to the Office of Emergency Planning and its Director; EO 11725 section 3 (effective July 1, 1973) transfers the authority then vested in the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness under this order to the Administrator of General Services. None of them revokes or terminates the order. Ending: EO 12148 section 5-106 revokes the order, effective July 15, 1979 by that order's own effective-date sentence (signed July 20, 1979). Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code search has two hits, a note under 42 U.S.C. 5195 reprinting EO 12148 with its section 5-106 revocation and the title 50 disposition table listing this order as omitted; the eCFR search has two hits for which the dossier holds no located text, so they were not relied on either way; the Federal Register catalog notes (five machine hits) record the amendments by EO 10773 and EO 11051, a cross-reference to EO 11725 and the revocation by EO 12148.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The order has no sunset or condition ending it. (2) EO 10773, EO 11051 and EO 11725 change which officer makes the national-defense determination or holds the authority; each is recorded as a later event, and none revokes or terminates the order. (3) The intervening statutory renamings of the mobilization office (from the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization, and from the Office of Emergency Planning to the Office of Emergency Preparedness) are not shown by any held source and do not name the order, so they are not recorded as events or ends. (4) No held source shows that the section 302 loan authority lapsed before 1979; that possibility is not excluded, but it is not supported by held evidence, and the order is permissive, so it is not treated as ended by disuse. (5) EO 12148 names the order and revokes it, effective July 15, 1979.","independent_command_check":"The loan authority itself is conferred by section 302 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, which the order invokes and which is not held in this packet. The order adds only the permission to use that authority for major-disaster facilities that the named officer determines are required for national defense; it creates no separate continuing command.","savings_check":"No savings wording in EO 12148 attaches to the revocation; loans already made are past transactions governed by their own terms and the statute.","scope_check":"One clause covers the whole order. EO 12148 section 5-106 revokes the order, as amended, without exception, so the whole order ends on that date."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12148 attaches no savings sentence to the section 5-106 revocation, and the held text contains no general savings clause (searched for saving, remain in, continue in, nothing in and notwithstanding). Loans already made would be governed by their own terms and by section 302 of the Defense Production Act, not by this order; no continuing right or duty arising only from the order is shown.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10843, signed 1959-10-09 (24 FR 8289), creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 ("create a Board of Inquiry"), gives it the powers and duties set forth in Title II of that Act, directs it to report to the President "on or before October 16,1959." and provides that after its report the board continues in existence until it is "terminated by the President". Later event: Executive Order 10848, signed 1959-10-14 (24 FR 8401, Federal Register of October 16, 1959), amends the second sentence in the penultimate paragraph of this order "to read as follows:" the Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of such Act on or before "October 19, 1959." Before the amendment the sentence ended "on or before October 16,1959."; after it the report date is October 19, 1959. The amendment moves a deadline by three days and leaves the creation of the board and its continued existence unchanged (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments); an amended report deadline is not an end. The only own-terms end is termination by the President. No held text records such a termination, and that absence is not proof that none occurred, so it is disclosed as an open earlier-end candidate; under the owner's report-deadline ruling an order of this kind that stayed on the books ends on its express revocation. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and" "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The cited source is the held Federal Register text of EO 12553; the dossier's located-provision records for the EO 12553 revocation of this order are American Presidency Project transcriptions, so they are not cited. The table on page 11 of the held text lists the number 10843 as entry 53 of 64 and 10848 as entry 54; on that page the text layer prints the numbers first and the subjects afterwards, and entry 53 of the subject list is "Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the steel industry", which agrees with the order's title. The alignment is by position, and a reviewer should confirm it against the page image. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective and take effect; the only hit is a word inside another order's subject line), so the signing date, 1986-02-25, is recorded; the filing date 1986-02-26 (the held text prints "Filed 2-26-86") and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 are the alternative readings, and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

Executive Order 10843
CREATING A BOARD OF INQUIRY  
TO REPORT ON A LABOR DIS­
PUTE AFFECTING THE STEEL IN­
DUSTRY OF THE UNITED STATES
WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute 
between certain corporations or organ­
izations in the United States producing 
or fabricating steel or the components 
thereof and certain of their employees 
represented by the United Steel Workers 
of America, AFL-CIO; and
WHEREAS such dispute has resulted 
in a strike which, in my opinion, affects 
a substantial part of the steel industry, 
an industry engaged in trade, commerce, 
and transportation among the several 
States and with foreign nations, and in 
the production of goods for commerce, 
and which strike will, if permitted to 
continue, imperil the national health 
and safety:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 206 
of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 
1947,61 Stat. 155 (29 U.S.C. 176), I hereby 
create a Board of Inquiry, consisting of 
George W. Taylor of Pennsylvania, 
Chairman, John Perkins of Delaware and 
Paul N. Lehoczky of Ohio as members 
to inquire into the issues involved in 
such dispute.
The Board shall have powers and 
duties as set forth in Title II of such Act. 
The Board shall report to the President 
in accordance with the provisions of sec­
tion 206 of such Act on or before October 16,1959.
Upon submission of its report, tl 
Board shall continue in existence to pe 
form such other functions as may be r 
Quired under such Act, until the Boa: 
ls terminated by the President.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10843 (24 FR 8289, Federal Register of October 13, 1959), signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower and dated October 9, 1959; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: one whole-order clause covers the heading, the two recitals and the operative text: creation of a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, with three named members, to inquire into the steel-industry dispute; the grant of the powers and duties set forth in Title II of that Act; the direction to report on or before October 16, 1959; and the provision that after its report the Board continues in existence until terminated by the President. Later event: EO 10848 (1959-10-14, 24 FR 8401) restates the report sentence with the date October 19, 1959. Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order and its amendment EO 10848 by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog notes (five machine hits) record the amendment by EO 10848 and the revocation by EO 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The report deadline, as amended by EO 10848, is a deadline and not an end; the board's actual report date is not shown by any held source. (2) The order's own contingent end is termination of the board by the President; no held text records such a termination, and that absence is not proof that none occurred, so it is disclosed as an open earlier-end candidate rather than claimed. (3) The OFR catalog notes and the number-citation scan of held texts show no instrument other than EO 10848 (an amendment) and EO 12553 (the revocation) acting on this order. Under the owner's report-deadline ruling an order of this kind ends on its express revocation, and EO 12553 is the first end shown by held evidence.","independent_command_check":"No command is independent of the board: its creation, powers, report and continued existence all concern the same Board of Inquiry, and the continued-existence clause ended with the order on revocation if not earlier by an unrecorded presidential termination. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The first scope is the order's recitals and section 1, signed 1961-01-24 (26 FR 781). The recitals are not operative commands. Section 1 amends Executive Order 10900 (administration of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954) by renumbering its sections 6 and 7 as sections 7 and 8 and inserting a new section 6, under which the Director of the Food-for-Peace Program, subject to the direction of the President, "shall be responsible for" the continuous supervision and coordination of the functions delegated or assigned by that order to officers or agencies of the Government. The renumbering was executed on issue; the inserted section continued as part of EO 10900. Later event 1: Executive Order 11252, signed 1965-10-20 (30 FR 13507), section 1: all functions of the Director of the Food-For-Peace Program, including those under EO 10900 as amended, "are hereby transferred to the Secretary of State; and that order" "and memorandum are modified accordingly." Section 4: "This order shall take effect on November 1,1965." Before: the coordinating responsibility in section 6 rested with the Director of the Food-for-Peace Program; after: the Director's functions rested with the Secretary of State. EO 11252 does not name EO 10915 or section 6 and prints no replacement text. Later event 2: Executive Order 11963, signed 1977-01-19 (42 FR 4325), section 2: EO 10900 is further amended by revoking section 5 and "redesignating Sections 6, 7 and 8 as Sections 5, 6 and" 7 respectively. On that date section 6 was the Food-for-Peace section inserted by this order (no held amendment renumbered EO 10900's sections between 1961 and 1977), so the inserted section was renumbered section 5 with its text unchanged. Before: section 6; after: section 5. EO 11963 has no effective-date wording, so its signing date is recorded; the publication date 1977-01-24 is the alternative reading. The redesignation shows the section was still part of EO 10900 in 1977, so the 1965 transfer is not treated as an end. First end: Executive Order 12220, Agricultural Trade Development, signed 1980-06-27 (45 FR 44245, Federal Register of July 1, 1980), section 1-501: "Executive Order N o. 10900 o f January 5,1961, as am ended, is revoked." EO 12220 has no effective-date wording (the held text was searched), so the signing date 1980-06-27 is recorded; the publication date 1980-07-01 is the alternative reading. The cited source is the held Federal Register text of EO 12220; the dossier's located-provision record for this pair is an American Presidency Project transcription and is not cited. The inserted section (section 5 since 1977) ended with that revocation.

Executive Order 11252
FOOD-FOR-PEACE PROGRAM
W H E R E A S the F ood-For-Peace Program has fulfilled and con­
tinues to fulfill the hopes of its creators and is providing the United 
States with a significant new medium for advancing the cause of 
world peace and understanding through the use of our agricultural 
abundance to alleviate hunger, malnutrition, and privation among 
our neighbors abroad ; and
W H E R E A S the objectives of the Food-For-Peace Program can 
now best be achieved by vesting responsibility for the Program in the 
Secretary of State, the Cabinet official chiefly responsible for our 
policies and programs abroad, so that the activities of this Program 
will be coordinated, consolidated, and carried out more effectively with 
related activities of the United States abroad; and
W H E R E A S the Secretary of State will be able to discharge these 
responsibilities more effectively through a special assistant specifically 
designated to assist him in carrying out the Food-For-Peace Program :
NOW, T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
subsection (f) of Section 303 of the Government Employees Salary 
Reform Act of 1964 and as President of the United States, it is hereby 
ordered as follows :
S ection  1. A ll functions of the Director of the Food-For-Peace 
Program, including those under Executive Order No. 10900 of Janu­
ary 5,1961, as amended, and under the Presidential memorandum of 
January 24, 1961, relating to the Food-For-Peace Program (26 F.R . 
781), are hereby transferred to the Secretary of State; and that order 
and memorandum are modified accordingly.

ant to the Secretary of State who shall assist the Secretary as the

Executive Order 10915
AMENDING PRIOR EXECUTIVE OR­
DERS TO PROVIDE FOR THE RE­
SPONSIBILITIES OF THE DIRECTOR  
OF THE FOOD-FOR-PEACE PRO­
GRAM
Whereas American agricultural abun­
dance offers a unique opportunity for  
the United States to promote the in­
terests of peace in a significant way and  
to play an important role in helping to  
provide a more adequate diet for peoples  
around the world; and
Whereas exports of farm products are  
of great importance to the domestic  
economy, furnishing approximately 11 
percent of total farm income; and
Whereas many government functions  
and activities relate to the movement  
overseas of agricultural products and  
commodities, and a number of govern­
ment agencies have responsibilities in  
connection with these activities; and
Whereas it is of fundamental im­
portance that we have a national food  
policy directed toward using our agricul­
tural abundance as a national asset to  
meet foreign policy objectives.
NOW , THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me as President of  
the United States, it is ordered as  
follows;
S e c t i o n 1. Executive Order No. 10900  
of January 5, 1961 (26 F.R. 143), headed  
“Administration of the Agricultural  
Trade Development and Assistance Act  
of 1954, as amended,” is hereby amended  
by renumbering sections 6 and 7 thereof  
as sections 7 and 8, respectively, and by  
inserting after section 5 the following  
new section 6:
“ Se c. 6. Director of the Food-for-Peace  
Program.  Subject to the direction of the  
President, the Director of the Food-for-  
Peace Program (provided for in a letter  
of the President bearing the same date  
as this order) shall be responsible for
the continuous supervision and coordi­
nation of the functions hereinabove dele­
gated or otherwise assigned to officers  
or agencies of the Government. The  
foregoing provisions of this section shall  
not be construed as terminating any  
delegation or other assignment of func­
tion made by other sections of this  
order.”

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The text of new section 111 of Executive Order 10893, inserted by section 2 of EO 10915, makes the Director of the Food-for-Peace Program, subject to the direction of the President, responsible for the continuous supervision and coordination of the functions under section 402 of the Act (22 U.S.C. 1922), without superseding any delegation made by the Act or by other sections of that order. It has the same end as section 2: Executive Order 10973 supersedes section 2 of EO 10915 by name (section 605, item (b)) and supersedes EO 10893 except Part II and one funding purpose (item (a)); section 111 was added at the end of Part I and concerns coordination of section 402 functions, so neither exception keeps it. Recorded end: 1961-09-30, the effective date stated in section 607 of EO 10973 ("as of September 30, 1961."), with the signing date 1961-11-03 as the alternative reading.

Executive Order 10915
AMENDING PRIOR EXECUTIVE OR­
DERS TO PROVIDE FOR THE RE­
SPONSIBILITIES OF THE DIRECTOR  
OF THE FOOD-FOR-PEACE PRO­
GRAM
Whereas American agricultural abun­
dance offers a unique opportunity for  
the United States to promote the in­
terests of peace in a significant way and  
to play an important role in helping to  
provide a more adequate diet for peoples  
around the world; and
Whereas exports of farm products are  
of great importance to the domestic  
economy, furnishing approximately 11 
percent of total farm income; and
Whereas many government functions  
and activities relate to the movement  
overseas of agricultural products and  
commodities, and a number of govern­
ment agencies have responsibilities in  
connection with these activities; and
Whereas it is of fundamental im­
portance that we have a national food  
policy directed toward using our agricul­
tural abundance as a national asset to  
meet foreign policy objectives.
NOW , THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me as President of  
the United States, it is ordered as  
follows;
S e c t i o n 1. Executive Order No. 10900  
of January 5, 1961 (26 F.R. 143), headed  
“Administration of the Agricultural  
Trade Development and Assistance Act  
of 1954, as amended,” is hereby amended  
by renumbering sections 6 and 7 thereof  
as sections 7 and 8, respectively, and by  
inserting after section 5 the following  
new section 6:
“ Se c. 6. Director of the Food-for-Peace  
Program.  Subject to the direction of the  
President, the Director of the Food-for-  
Peace Program (provided for in a letter  
of the President bearing the same date  
as this order) shall be responsible for
the continuous supervision and coordi­
nation of the functions hereinabove dele­
gated or otherwise assigned to officers  
or agencies of the Government. The  
foregoing provisions of this section shall  
not be construed as terminating any  
delegation or other assignment of func­
tion made by other sections of this  
order.”
Sec. 2. Executive Order No. 10893 of 
November 8,1960 (25 F.R. 10731) , headed  
“Administration of mutual security and  
related functions,” is hereby amended  
by adding at the end of Part I thereof a  
new section 111, reading as follows;
Sec. 111. Director of the Food-for-  
Peace Program.  Subject to the direction  
of the President, the Director of the  
Food-for-Peace Program shall be re­
sponsible for the continuous supervision  
and coordination of the functions under  
Section 402 of the Act (22 U.S.C. 1922). 
The foregoing provisions of this section  
shall not be construed as superseding  
any delegation or other assignment of  
function made by the Act or by other  
sections of this order.”

ing Annual Report Forms O, W ire-tele-  
graph and Ocean-cable Carriers, and R,  
Radiotelegraph Carriers.
The consolidation ordered herein is  
designed to make no change in any re­
porting requirement of substance. The  
separate report form designations, Form  
O, and Form R, are retained but will  
henceforth indicate a single document.  
Certain obsolete schedules or those  
which call for information which ex­
perience has shown the carriers have  
nothing to report on, and are not likely  
to have in the future, have been deleted.
The reporting requirements contained  
in the two annual report forms, Form O  
and Form R, were found to be so similar  
that it seemed a natural step to combine  
them and this similarity made it possible  
to combine many of the schedules in the  
two Forms even to the extent of retain­
ing schedule numbers and titles. There  
are, however, instances of such varia­
tions in the account classifications be­
tween wire-telegraph and ocean-cable,  
on the one hand, and radiotelegraph, on  
the other, that retention of separate re­
porting schedules was found necessary.
The pages of the new combined report  
form are numbered consecutively for  
more ready reference. The size of the  
sheets is the same as in telephone Annual  
Report Form M  prescribed by the Com­
mission and in the Form O  being  
superseded.
Combining of the two report forms  
ordered herein will contribute to. econ­
omy in printing and stocking as com­
pared to the costs of two totally separate  
documents.
A comparative table showing the dis­
position made of the schedules and other  
sheets contained in Forms O  and R  is  
attached to this order .1
It appearing that the consolidation of  
Annual Report Forms O and R  does not  
change in any material respect the re­
porting requirements of the carriers and  
hence that compliance with the public  
notice, procedural, and effective date re­
quirements of section 4 of the Adminis­
trative Procedure Act is unnecessary;  
and
It further appearing that consolida­
tion of the two Forms referred to is  
desirable;
1  F iled as p a rt o f the origin al docum ent.

tained in sections 4(i) and 219  of

forth hereinabove and in the attached  
Appendix 1 and a copy of which report  
form is available at the Offices of the  
Commission.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10915 (26 FR 781, Federal Register of January 26, 1961), signed by John F. Kennedy and dated January 24, 1961; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: I confirm the dossier's three scopes: (1) the recitals and section 1, which amends EO 10900 by renumbering its sections 6 and 7 as 7 and 8 and inserting a new section 6 (Director of the Food-for-Peace Program); (2) section 2, the command amending EO 10893 by adding a new section 111 at the end of its Part I; (3) the text of section 111 itself. Ends: section 2 and section 111 end on 1961-09-30, when EO 10973 section 605(b) supersedes section 2 of EO 10915 by name and section 605(a) supersedes EO 10893 except Part II and one funding purpose (section 607 makes EO 10973 effective as of September 30, 1961). The inserted section 6 of EO 10900 ends on 1980-06-27, when EO 12220 section 1-501 revokes EO 10900 as amended. Later events on the inserted section 6: EO 11252 (effective 1965-11-01) transfers all functions of the Director of the Food-for-Peace Program, including those under EO 10900 as amended, to the Secretary of State and modifies that order accordingly; EO 11963 section 2 (1977-01-19) revokes section 5 of EO 10900 and redesignates sections 6, 7 and 8 as sections 5, 6 and 7, so the inserted Food-for-Peace section became section 5. The whole-order end is the latest clause end, 1980-06-27. The dossier's missing items were resolved by reading the held texts: EO 10924 section 4 says it does not supersede or derogate from EO 10893; EO 11963 was read in full, and EO 12148 and EO 12220 were searched for every provision naming EO 10900. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog notes (four machine hits) record the partial supersession by EO 10973 and notes naming EO 11963 and EO 12148 as amending.

EO 10924 section 4 states that it does not supersede EO 10893 and is not an event. EO 12163 (effective October 1, 1979) later revoked what remained of EO 10893, after the 1961 end, so it does not change these dates. Section 1 and the inserted section 6: EO 11252 transferred the Director's functions to the Secretary of State and modified EO 10900 accordingly, without naming EO 10915 or printing replacement text; EO 11963 section 2 later redesignated the same section as section 5, which shows that the section was still part of EO 10900 in 1977, so EO 11252 is recorded as a later event and not as an end. The other amendments of EO 10900 in the held corpus change other parts of that order and leave the inserted section unchanged: EO 10972 (section 4(d)), EO 11036 (sections 4(a), 4(d)(5) and 4(d)(7)), EO 11051 section 601 (references to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization), EO 11963 section 1 (a new subsection (d) of section 1), EO 12148 section 5-107 (revocation of section 4(d)(2)) and EO 12163 section 1-903(b)(4) (a new subsection of section 3). savings_residuals.reason: Section 606 of EO 10973 ("Saving provisions.") continues determinations, orders and other actions taken with respect to any function affected by that order, and not revoked or made inapplicable before its date, until amended, modified or terminated by appropriate authority. Actions taken under section 111 are therefore accrued effects; they do not keep section 111 operative. The functions of the Director under section 6 of EO 10900 were transferred to the Secretary of State by EO 11252; EO 12220 has no savings clause of its own.

Sec. 301. Enlisted members who are being subsisted in kind in a mess 
and whose duties require them to be absent from their station during 
one or more meals shall be entitled for each such meal to a pro-rated 
share of the daily basic allowance for subsistence authorized for 
members on duty at stations where rations in kind are not available. 
The Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the 
Secretary of Commerce are hereby authorized to establish the amount 
of the pro-rated share of the daily basic allowance for subsistence 
applicable to each one of the three daily meals, which amount shall 
be uniform for all the services concerned. The total of the amounts 
of the shares for the three daily meals shall not exceed the amount of 
the basic daily allowance for subsistence authorized by section 402 of 
title 37 of the United States Code. ‘

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause (amendment 2, striking the words and (3) in section 3 of EO 10168 and inserting a reference to clauses (3), (5) and (6), with the sentence making the amendments effective as of the first day of the first month after the month of issue) terminated on 1964-06-22 when Executive Order 11157 (29 FR 7973, Federal Register of June 24, 1964) revoked Executive Order 10989 by number in section 502. The revoking sentence is "The following Executive orders are revoked:" and the item naming this order is "(k) Executive Order No. 10989 of January 22,1962." research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10989 (27 FR 727, Federal Register of January 25, 1962), signed by John F. Kennedy and dated January 22, 1962; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier's three clauses (the lead-in, amendment 1 adding clauses (5) and (6) to section 2(a), and amendment 2 changing section 3 together with the effective-date sentence) are contiguous and cover every operative sentence; I confirm the inventory. The order further amends Executive Order 10168 of October 11, 1950, as amended (additional pay for sea and foreign duty of enlisted members): it adds two clauses treating duty on an artificial island such as a Texas Tower on the outer Continental Shelf as sea duty (clause (5) for assignment there, clause (6) for duty there of eight consecutive days or more while based ashore), amends section 3 to refer to clauses (3), (5) and (6), and makes the amendments effective as of the first day of the first month after the month of issue, that is 1962-02-01. Ending: Executive Order 11157 of June 22, 1964, section 502, revokes this order as item (k) and EO 10168 itself as item (c). The cited source is the held Federal Register text of EO 11157; the dossier's located-provision records for this pair that use a transcription mirror are not cited. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 11157 and the matching note on EO 11157 naming this order. EO 12553 does not list 10989 and no catalog note links them.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 11013, signed 1962-04-07 (27 FR 3373), creates under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 a Board of Inquiry of three named members to inquire into the issues in the maritime dispute described in its recitals, gives it the powers and duties set forth in Title II of that Act, directs it to report to the President "on or before April 11, 1962." and provides that upon submission of its report the Board continues in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act, "until the Board is terminated by the President." The order contains no standstill or status-quo provision. The report date is a deadline, not an end, and the actual report date is not shown by any held source. The only own-terms end is termination by the President; no held source records it, and it is disclosed as an open earlier-end candidate rather than claimed. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and" "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" Its table on page 12 of the held text prints this order as the one-line row "11013 Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the maritime industry", which agrees with the order's title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective and take effect; the only hit is a word inside another order's subject line), so the signing date, 1986-02-25, is recorded; the filing date 1986-02-26 (the held text prints "Filed 2-26-86") and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 are the alternative readings, and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

Executive Order 11013
CREATING A BOARD OF INQUIRY TO REPORT ON A LABOR DISPUTE  
AFFECTING THE MARITIME INDUSTRY OF THE UNITED STATES
WHEREAS, there exists a labor dispute between certain-ship owners 
and operators in the United States foreign and domestic trades and 
certain of their employees represented by: the Sailors’  Union of the 
Pacific; Pacific -  Coast Marine Firemen, Oilers, Watertenders and 
»Vipers Association 5 and the Marine Cooks and Stewards Union; and
WHEREAS, such dispute has resulted in a strike which, in my 
opinion, affects a substantial part of the maritime industry, an indus­
try engaged in trade, commerce, and transportation among the several 
States and with foreign nations, and which strike will, if permitted 
to continue, imperil the national health and safety:
NOW THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, 61 Stat. 
155 (29 USC. 176), I  hereby create a Board of Inquiry, consisting of 
Professor James J. Healy, Chairman, Professor Frank J. Dugan, 
and Honorable Laurence E. Seibel as members to inquire into the 
issues involved in such dispute.
The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title I I  of 
such Act. -  The Board shall report to the President in accordance with 
the provisions of section 206 of such Act on or before April 11, 1962.
Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence 
to perform such other functions as may be required under such Act, 
until the Board is terminated by the President.
_T T  -  J ohn  F. K ennedy
I he  W hite  H ouse,
April 7,1962.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11013 (27 FR 3373, Federal Register of April 10, 1962), signed by John F. Kennedy and dated April 7, 1962; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: one whole-order clause covers the heading, the two recitals and the operative text, which is a Labor Management Relations Act, 1947, section 206 board of inquiry order with no Railway Labor Act content and no status-quo or standstill sentence. Its commands are: creation of a Board of Inquiry of three named members to inquire into the issues in the maritime dispute; the grant of the powers and duties set forth in Title II of that Act; the direction to report to the President on or before April 11, 1962; and the provision that upon submission of its report the Board continues in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act until the Board is terminated by the President. Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 12553 and the matching note on EO 12553. The held-text number-citation scan found the number only on the order's own Federal Register page.

EO 12220 has no effective-date wording, so the signing date 1980-06-27 is recorded; the publication date 1980-07-01 is the alternative reading.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11036 (27 FR 6653, Federal Register of July 13, 1962), signed by John F. Kennedy and dated July 11, 1962; number, date and subject agree with the census register (Administration of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954, as amended). Inventory: the dossier splits the order into two contiguous clauses at an OCR break inside the substituted section 4(a)(1) (the second clause begins with a sentence fragment labelled Section 104). Together they cover amendments (I), (II) and (III) and the signature; I confirm the inventory as complete and decide both clauses as parts of one amending order. The order further amends Executive Order 10900 of January 5, 1961, as amended: (I) it substitutes a new section 4(a), under which foreign currencies accruing under Title I may be used for section 104 purposes, the Director of the Bureau of the Budget fixes the amounts and notifies the Secretary of the Treasury, and the section 104 waiver function is delegated to the Secretary of State for section 104(e) and to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget otherwise; (II) it inserts a new paragraph (5) in section 4(d) assigning section 104(s) purposes to the Department of the Treasury in consultation with the Department of State and delegating the terms-and-conditions function to the Secretary of the Treasury; (III) it substitutes a new section 4(d)(7) assigning section 104(g) purposes to the Department of State and delegating the loan-manner function to the Secretary of State. Ending: EO 12220 section 1-501 revokes EO 10900 as amended on 1980-06-27. The cited source is the held Federal Register text of EO 12220; the dossier's located-provision record for this pair is an American Presidency Project transcription and is not cited. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the note on this order recording its revocation by EO 12220 and the note recording this order's amendment of EO 10900. EO 12553 does not list 11036 (its held text was searched).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order's own text sets no end. Each intervening instrument in the dossier was checked against the held texts: Executive Order 11252 (1965-10-20) transfers the functions of the Director of the Food-For-Peace Program to the Secretary of State and modifies EO 10900 accordingly, but the functions amended here run to the Budget Director, the Treasury and State, not to that Director; Executive Order 11963 (1977-01-19) adds a subsection (d) to section 1 of EO 10900 and revokes and renumbers other sections; Executive Order 12148 (1979-07-20), in section 5-107, revokes only section 4(d)(2) of EO 10900, a paragraph this order does not touch (section 5-108 of EO 12148 revokes EO 10952); Executive Order 12163 (1979-09-29), in section 1-903(b)(4), adds a subsection to section 3 of EO 10900. None of these changes the text this order inserted, so none is an event or end for these clauses. The held text of Executive Order 11836, which the dossier lists as citing this order by number, prints the number 11036 over a different subject (the Transportation Cargo Security Program) and mentions neither EO 10900 nor the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act, so it is not an event for this order. The first end shown by held evidence is section 1-501 of EO 12220, effective 1980-06-27.","independent_command_check":"Each clause only amends EO 10900; none is a command independent of that order. The parent order was revoked as a whole by section 1-501 of EO 12220, so no surviving parent text carries these amendments.","savings_check":"Functions of the same kinds were delegated anew in sections 1-401 and 1-405 of EO 12220, which also revoked the parent; no continuing command of this order outside that new delegation was found, and EO 12220 has no express savings clause.","scope_check":"Two clauses cover the whole order; amendments (I), (II) and (III) were all part of EO 10900 as amended and ended together when EO 12220 revoked that order as amended."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12220, which revoked EO 10900 as amended, delegates functions of the same kinds anew: section 1-401(a) on the use of foreign currencies, with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget fixing the amounts and notifying the Secretary of the Treasury; section 1-401(b) delegating the section 104 waiver function to the Director of the United States International Development Cooperation Agency for section 104(e) and to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget otherwise; section 1-405(a) delegating the function of determining the manner in which loans under paragraph (f) of section 104 shall be made; section 1-405(b) delegating the function of prescribing terms and conditions under paragraph (j) of section 104 to the Secretary of the Treasury in consultation with the Secretary of State. EO 12220 cites paragraphs (f) and (j) where this order cited 104(g) and 104(s); whether those are the same statutory paragraphs relettered is not shown by a held statute and is not relied on. EO 12220 has no express savings clause, and no U.S. Code, eCFR or catalog hit shows any other continuing effect of this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 11138, signed 1964-01-07 (29 FR 225), waives for Frederick Strauss the section 1 leave-of-absence limit and the section 3(a) reemployment-rights limit of Executive Order 9721, as amended by Executive Order 10103, and provides that he shall be considered to have been on leave of absence "for the period August 12, 1957, through September 16, 1962," for all rights and benefits under EO 9721, as amended. Its parents had been revoked in 1959 by EO 10804 section 2 except for employees serving with an international organization on the enactment date of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act who did not elect coverage under it, and for vested rights; this order operates within that saved scope as the President framed it, and held evidence does not show whether Mr. Strauss elected coverage. Whether the waiver was used, and so exhausted, is not established by held evidence and is disclosed as open, not claimed. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and" "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" Its table on page 12 of the held text prints this order as the one-line row "11138 Modifying provisions for the transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations"; page 10 prints "10103 Amending provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations", and the number 9721 appears in the table on page 9. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective and take effect; the only hit is a word inside another order's subject line), so the signing date, 1986-02-25, is recorded; the filing date 1986-02-26 (the held text prints "Filed 2-26-86") and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 are the alternative readings, and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11138 (29 FR 225, Federal Register of January 9, 1964), signed by Lyndon B. Johnson and dated January 7, 1964; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers every operative sentence; I confirm it. The order modifies Executive Order 9721 of May 10, 1946, as amended by Executive Order 10103 of February 1, 1950 (transfer of personnel to public international organizations): it waives, for one named person, Frederick Strauss, the section 1 limit on the period during which a transferred employee is considered on leave of absence and the section 3(a) limit on the time within which reemployment rights may be exercised, and provides that he shall be considered to have been on leave of absence from August 12, 1957 through September 16, 1962 for the purpose of all rights and benefits provided by EO 9721, as amended. Parent order: Executive Order 10804 of February 12, 1959 (24 FR 1147, held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10804.txt), section 2, revoked EO 9721 and EO 10103, except that "each shall be considered to" remain in effect for any employee subject to it who was serving with an international organization on the date of enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act and did not elect coverage under that Act, and for rights and benefits vested before that date. EO 11138 was issued after that revocation and modifies EO 9721 only for one employee whose deemed leave began on August 12, 1957, before the 1958 Act; the President thus treated EO 9721 as still applying to him within the saved scope. The held evidence does not show the enactment date of the Act (EO 10804 cites it as 72 Stat. 961) or whether Mr. Strauss elected coverage under it; if he had, the saved parent would not have applied to him and the waiver would have had no field of operation. That question bears on the waiver's effect, not on whether this order stayed on the books, and EO 10804, being earlier, cannot be an end of this 1964 order. EO 12553 revoked EO 9721, EO 10103 and this order on the same day. Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 12553 and the matching note on EO 12553 naming this order.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No held source shows a revocation, supersession or expiry of this order before EO 12553; its own text has no end date or condition, and the waiver covers a past period and two time limits rather than a future event. Whether the waiver was used, and so exhausted by performance, is not established by held evidence: no held source shows whether or when Mr. Strauss exercised reemployment rights or claimed benefits under it (owner ruling 2026-10-28: an unestablished event is not claimed as an interval). The 1959 revocation of the parent orders by EO 10804, with its saving for employees serving on the enactment date of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act and for vested rights, came before this order and cannot end it; this order operated, as the President framed it, within that saved scope. The first end shown by held evidence is the express revocation by number in EO 12553, effective 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"The order's only command is the waiver and deeming rule for the named person; there is no independent continuing command. The parent EO 9721 did not continue generally after 1959: EO 10804 section 2 revoked it and EO 10103, keeping them in effect only for employees serving with an international organization on the enactment date of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act who did not elect coverage under it, and for rights vested before that date; EO 12553 then revoked both parents in 1986.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception. The deemed leave status for 1957-1962 is an accrued consequence; no held source shows a later right or duty depending on this order after 1986-02-25.","scope_check":"Single clause, whole order, one named person. EO 12553 revokes the whole order by its own row, and also revokes the parent orders EO 9721 and EO 10103 on the same day."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 amends section 1 of EO 11189 by adding the item that follows it (the Level IV addition). It ended with the whole order: first end Executive Order 12060, signed 1978-05-15 (43 FR 21315, Federal Register of May 17, 1978), whose section 3 provides that Executive Order No. 11189 of November 23, 1964, Executive Order No. 11195 of January 30, 1965, and Executive Order No. 11995 of June 8, 1977 "are revoked." EO 12060 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, 1978-05-15; the filing date 1978-05-16 and publication date 1978-05-17 are the alternative readings. The amendment continued until the amended order ended, and EO 11189 was revoked by the same sentence. Earlier candidate end that does not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; it is not the end because it does not name EO 11195): Pub. L. 89-554 (Sept. 6, 1966, 80 Stat. 378), which enacted title 5 of the United States Code, lists in 5 U.S.C. 5315 "(73) Chief of Protocol, Department of State." and in 5 U.S.C. 5316 item (101), the Assistant Director (Program Planning, Analysis and Research), Office of Economic Opportunity, "(110) General Counsel of the Veterans' Administration." and "(114) Staff Director, Commission on Civil Rights.", so every position this order added appears in the statute (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11195_Pub._L._89-554_Sept._6_1966_80_Stat._378_et_seq._including_5_U.S.C._5315_and_5316_as__c629b8a1e7.txt; it is not an evidence record of this dossier, so it is pinned here by path). The Federal Register catalog note on EO 11189 says that order was "Nullified by 80 Stat. 460, 461 (5 U.S.C. 5315, 5316)" because the statute included all positions added by EO 11189 and its amendment EO 11195 (jobs/later-events/output/CATALOG_INDEX.csv), but the catalog note on EO 11195 itself records only the EO 12060 revocation. Section 7(c) of the same Act provides that an order in effect under a replaced law continues in effect under the corresponding provision "until repealed, amended, or superseded.", which points the other way. I did not establish that the statute extinguished this order, so EO 12060 is recorded as the first end.

Presidential Documents
Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 11195
PLACING ADDITIONAL POSITIONS IN LEVELS IV AND V OF THE  
FEDERAL EXECUTIVE SALARY SCHEDULE
By virtue of the authority vested in me by subsection (g) of Section 
303 of the Government Employees Salary Reform Act of 1964, and as 
President of the United States, it is ordered as follows :
Section  1. Section 1 of Executive Order 11189 of November 23, 
1964, is amended by adding thereto the following :
(6) Chief of Protocol, Department of State.
Sec. 2. Section 2 of Executive Order 11189 of November 23,1964, is 
amended by adding thereto the following :
(15) Staff Director, Commission on Civil Rights.
(16) Assistant Director (Program Planning, Analysis, and Re­
search), Office of Economic Opportunity.
(17) General Counsel, Veterans Administration.
Sec. 3. This Order shall be effective immediately.
T h e W h ite H ouse,
January 30 ,  1965.
L yndon  B. J ohnson
